'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]], [[Russia–NATO relations]]
***[[President of the United States|US President]] [[Joe Biden]] says a full-scale Russian invasion of [[Ukraine]] will result in a more severe penalty than a "minor incursion" as he predicts that [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] "will move in [on Ukraine]; he has to do something". [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/blinken-says-russian-attack-ukraine-could-come-very-short-notice-2022-01-19/ (Reuters)]
***[[United States Secretary of State|US Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] arrives in [[Kyiv]], Ukraine, in a show of support for Ukraine. During a one-day visit, Blinken will meet with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]]. [[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] said yesterday that "[[Russia]] could at any point launch an attack on Ukraine" and that "No option is off the table". [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20220119-blinken-arrives-in-ukraine-in-show-of-solidarity-as-fears-grow-of-russian-invasion (France 24)]
***[[Lithuania]]n [[Ministry of National Defence (Lithuania)|Defence Minister]] [[Arvydas Anušauskas]] warns that the presence of [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian troops]] in [[Belarus]] poses a "direct threat" to Lithuania. [https://www.politico.eu/article/russian-troops-in-belarus-are-direct-threat-to-lithuania-defense-minister/ (''Politico.eu'')]
***The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Royal Air Force]] continues flights to [[Ukraine]] delivering "thousands" of [[MBT LAW]] [[Anti-tank warfare|anti-tank missiles]] to the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]]. Russia accuses Britain of "fuelling the crisis" by sending lethal weapons to Ukraine. [https://ukdefencejournal.org.uk/third-day-of-british-weapon-flights-to-ukraine/ (UK Defence Journal)] [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/britain-fears-tens-of-thousands-dead-if-russia-invades-ukraine-jvzh266pr (''The Times'')]
 
'''Business and economy'''
*Employees of the [[Societatea de Transport București|STB]], [[Bucharest]]'s largest public transport company, go on strike demanding the resignation of its chairman, Adrian Criț. The city authorities, led by the [[Save Romania Union]]-backed mayor [[Nicușor Dan]], condemn the strike, blaming it on the [[Social Democratic Party (Romania)|Social Democratic Party]]-backed trade unionist Vasile Petrariu as an attempt to undermine his authority. [https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/directorul-stb-greva-e-ilegala-cer-in-instanta-suspendarea-ei-un-sofer-a-iesit-pe-traseu-a-fost-sunat-de-sindicalisti-si-s-a-intors-1808985 (Digi24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Six people are killed in a fire at a nursing home in [[Moncada, Valencia]], Spain. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/nursing-home-fire-kills-5-in-eastern-spain/2022/01/19/d6e3faf0-78f7-11ec-9dce-7313579de434_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*Twenty-nine people are killed during a [[stampede]] at an open-air [[Pentecostalism|Pentecostal]] church in [[Monrovia]], [[Liberia]]. The stampede was triggered by panic after gangsters entered the prayer ground after a collection. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-60070025 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Japan]]ese [[Government of Japan|government]] announces that it will place [[Tokyo]] and 12 other [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s under a quasi-[[state of emergency]] from January 21 to February 13 amid an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases due to the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]], with the country reporting a record for the second consecutive day of 41,487 new cases of COVID-19. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2022/01/147dc2616a69-japan-set-to-put-tokyo-12-other-areas-under-covid-quasi-emergency.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports its first confirmed deaths related to the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in two unvaccinated people in their 60s who had underlying health conditions. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/01/19/22/philippines-reports-first-2-deaths-from-omicron-variant (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports its first three locally transmitted cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in [[Ho Chi Minh City]]. [http://www.hanoitimes.vn/vietnam-confirms-first-community-cases-of-omicron-319803.html (''Hanoi Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 11,181 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 841,785. [http://www.bta.bg/en/c/DF/id/2556986 (Bulgarian Press Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Government of the Czech Republic|Czech government]] suspends plans to make COVID-19 vaccination mandatory for key workers and people over the age of 60, which was expected to come into effect in March. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/czech-government-dismisses-mandate-vaccination-plan-82352700 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 112,323 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-germany-logs-more-than-100000-cases-for-first-time/a-60469878 (Deutsche Welle)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in American Samoa]]
****A seventh passenger from a [[Hawaiian Airlines]] flight from [[Honolulu]], [[Hawaii]], tests positive for COVID-19. The plane landed in [[American Samoa]] on January 6, 2022. [https://samoanews.com/local-news/seventh-passenger-jan-6-flight-tests-positive-and-isolation (Samoa News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kiribati]]
****[[Kiribati]] announces a curfew and mandatory face masks after 36 passengers on a [[charter flight]] from [[Fiji]] test positive for COVID-19 upon arrival. The plane was the first international commercial flight to land in the country since March 2020. Kiribati reopened its borders on January 10th. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/world/south-pacific/127540485/covid19-kiribati-confirms-37-cases-makes-maskwearing-mandatory (Stuff.co.nz)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
***The [[Algeria]]n [[Government of Algeria|government]] announces that all elementary and high schools will be closed for 10 days due to an increase in the number of [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]] cases in the country. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2007851/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***[[Mexico]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 60,552 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4,495,310. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-20/mexico-covid-cases-rise-by-record-that-doubles-previous-wave (Bloomberg)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Westminster lockdown parties controversy]]
**[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] [[Member of parliament|MP]] [[Christian Wakeford]] [[Crossing the floor|crosses the floor]] to the opposition [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], stating that [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]'s behaviour has been "disgraceful". There are growing calls within the ruling Conservative Party for Johnson to resign amid public outrage over "Partygate". [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/lawmaker-uk-pm-johnsons-party-defects-opposition-2022-01-19/ (Reuters)]
